title: Minor Keys with Sharps

expected.notes: One part (Violoncello), bass clef, 16 bars of 3/4, 4 systems.  Eight harmonic-minor keys, 2 bars each: A minor (bars 1-2), E (3-4), B (5-6), F# (7-8), C# (9-10), G# (11-12), D# (13-14), A# minor (15-16).  The raised leading note in bar 2 of each segment is a printed accidental: G#, D#, A#, E#, B# (sharps) and F##, C##, G## (double sharps in G#, D#, A# minor).  Key signatures are read in bass clef.  <mode> (major/minor) is encoded but is not printed: a key signature looks the same for the major key and its relative minor, so evaluators should compare <fifths> and treat mode as unobservable.

count_conventions.clef-*: initial clef of every staff + every clef change (system-start reprints and courtesy clefs not counted)
count_conventions.clef-change: clef elements after the initial clefs
count_conventions.key-*: initial key + every key change (system-start reprints and courtesy key signatures not counted); key-0 = no sharps/flats
count_conventions.key-change: key elements after measure 1; x-key-cancel = key changes that print cancellation naturals
count_conventions.key-* / time-* / key-change per part: counted per MusicXML <key>/<time> element, i.e. once per part: a multi-staff part (piano, organ) has one <key> for all its staves, so the printed signatures are N_staves times more numerous
count_conventions.time-*: time signature statements (time-common / time-cut replace time-4-4 / time-2-2 when the symbol is used)
count_conventions.ledger-above / ledger-below: noteheads needing >= 1 ledger line (displayed staff position >= 6 or <= -6 half-spaces from the middle line, after clef / clef-octave-change / ottava)
count_conventions.acc-courtesy: accidentals with cautionary="yes" (also counted under their glyph tag); x-acc-courtesy-paren = the parenthesised subset
count_conventions.x-acc-natural-sharp / x-acc-natural-flat: LilyPond "extra natural" before a single sharp/flat that follows a double sharp/flat in the same bar (natural-sharp / natural-flat)
count_conventions.system-break / page-break: explicit <print new-system/new-page> in the first part

notes: Courtesy clefs / key signatures / time signatures printed at the end of a system before a change are not separate MusicXML elements (they are implied by the change in the next measure) and are not counted.
Clefs and key signatures reprinted at every system start are implied in MusicXML and not counted; counts cover the initial statement of every staff and every change.
Stem directions and beams in the truth are copied from the instrumented LilyPond render and cross-checked (stems, flags, beam groups); they describe this engraving.
System breaks are explicit in the engraving and encoded as <print new-system="yes"/>.
<mode> (major/minor) is encoded but is not printed: a key signature looks the same for the major key and its relative minor, so evaluators should compare <fifths> and treat mode as unobservable.
